description: Fingerprint the exact GPU you're running on, even among identical GPUs, from the order its atomic adds land in. 99.1% accuracy, survives reboots, can't be faked, and a default torch.index_add_ call leaks it.
readme_excerpt: # Telling identical GPUs apart Blog post: Telling identical GPUs apart from their numerical output **Two GPUs of the same model compute the same sum in a slightly different order, and that difference is enough to tell them apart.** A small CUDA kernel identifies which of 19 identical NVIDIA A40s it ran on with 99.1% accuracy, using only the numbers it computes. It reads no serial number and uses no timers. - **It survives reboots.** After a container restart, all 12 measurements matched the right chip. - **It couldn't be forged.** An attacker on one chip, tuning every launch setting it controls, reached at best 0.616 correlation with another chip's fingerprint. Genuine chips match their own at 0.946 on average, and never below 0.916. - **A default `torch.index_add_` call leaks it too.** Reading nothing but that op's ordinary output identifies the chip with 100% accuracy among GPUs on the same driver, and 78% across mixed drivers. - **It works across models:** A40, RTX 3090, RTX 4090 and L40S. Why it works: when thousands of thread blocks race to update one counter, the hardware decides who arrives first. Tiny manufacturing differences between a chip's cores bias that order the same way every time. PyTorch's deterministic mode removes the `index_add_` leak. readme_excerpt: # diff-soup: differentiable, sparse-oriented unified PDE suite diff-soup is a software package written in JAX for modeling, simulation, and inference of (stiff) dynamical systems governed by ODEs, DAEs, and PDEs. For modeling: - a Recipe API that states equations in math-like notation on structured and unstructured domains; - finite difference, finite volume and finite element discretizations; - sparse Jacobians assembled by automatic differentiation with graph coloring. For simulation: - three variable-step, variable-order stiff integrators written in JAX, `JNDF`, `JBDF` and `JIDA`, for ODEs and DAEs up to index one; - sparse direct solves with NVIDIA cuDSS on the GPU, and KLU or dense solves on the CPU; - forward and reverse mode differentiation of every solve, to second order; - batched solves, with data and model parallelism across GPUs and cluster nodes. For inference: - parameter estimation using least squares estimation, maximum likelihood estimation (MLE), and maximum a posteriori (MAP) estimation; - physically-constrained deep learning using differentiable simulation, with neural networks embedded inside the physical model. readme_excerpt: # bootgpt A neural network that boots your PC. The MBR is 512 bytes of hand written asm. It loads an 11.5 KB int8 model from the next 23 sectors and runs it in 16-bit real mode on a 386. No OS, no C runtime, nothing. The machine wakes up and dreams a Linux boot log: timestamps, PCI bars, ACPI events for hardware that never existed. demo Build thread: With 8 chars of context and one hidden layer this is roughly the quality you get: ``` [ 2.283888] pci 0000:01:01.4: [1b36:0a35] ryndrde c4128 6422 Vveine [ 1.953886] pci 0000:01:1f.2: reg 0x10: [mem 0x7e4515e5-0x2d766c27] usbbore: reg [ 0.206596] Command line: BOOT_IMAGE=/vmlinu -5.5.2-1-generic gcc version 13.3.0, GNU ld ... [ 1.815765] ACPI: PCI Interrupt Link [LNKA: v/s.xos212 [ 1.883084] NET: Registered protocol family 16 ``` ## Run it ``` brew install nasm qemu python3 -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/pip install numpy ./build.sh ./run.sh ``` disk.img is a normal boot image. dd it to a USB stick and boot any BIOS box if you have one. It only reads its own sectors. ## Pieces `corpus_gen.py` makes 3 MB of fake dmesg. readme_excerpt: # NablaEngine **Fast, exact simulation gradients for the Unitree G1.** *Pronounced "Nabla Engine".* Time per 20 ms control step for 4096 Unitree G1 worlds on one NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000: the forward step, and one step with its gradient from the input state. NablaEngine is a differentiable GPU physics engine for the Unitree G1 humanoid. It simulates thousands of worlds per call with MuJoCo's physics and returns analytic gradients of every step with respect to the state and the actions, for first-order policy learning, trajectory optimization and system identification. readme_excerpt: # HOPE: Hilbert Operator for Progressive Encoding & DEFT Transfer Learning This repository contains the reference implementations of **HOPE** (*Hilbert Operator for Progressive Encoding*) and **DEFT** (*Dispersed Elastic Fine-Tuning*): 1. **Data-Free Progressive Model Compression (`hope.py`, `compress_resnet50.py`, `hope_baselines.py`, `plot_compression_curves.py`):** HOPE compresses an ImageNet-pretrained ResNet-50 (Keras) through a sequence of analytical steps (pruning a neuron via `PRUNE`, merging two neurons into one synthesized parent neuron via `MERGE`, or evicting the residual branch of a bottleneck block via `EVICT`), selected greedily by a rate-distortion criterion. Every step is recorded together with the information needed to undo it. The resulting *curriculum* lets the compressed network be decoded step by step to any intermediate density, or all the way back to the pretrained network (lossless up to float32 round-off). HOPE is strictly data-free: every cost is evaluated in closed form from the weights and the stored BatchNorm parameters and statistics. It uses no training images, no calibration data, and no fine-tuning; ImageNet is only needed to measure the accuracy of the compressed networks. readme_excerpt: # One-time vault for Bitcoin Google Quantum AI estimates that a first-generation quantum computer, primed in advance, could break a Bitcoin key about nine minutes after it appears, a chance of slightly under 41% to steal an ordinary spend before the next block confirms it. This script makes it break **a hundred keys** in that window instead. No fork, no new opcode, no private miner involvement: Bitcoin Core default relay policy accepts it as standard. It works today, a spend costs about 2,759 vbytes, and signing takes milliseconds. It's making a quantum attacker work harder. **It is not quantum-safe.** It is a work factor, the cheapest speed bump available until Bitcoin can verify post-quantum signatures. That takes more than BIP-360: its Pay-to-Merkle-Root outputs remove Taproot's exposed key-path spend, but a script-path spend still signs with ECDSA or Schnorr and reveals its keys in flight, so a separate post-quantum signature mechanism, such as the hash-based BIP-SHRINCS draft, is needed as well. > Status: experimental, unaudited. readme_excerpt: # libstrix HIP kernels tuned for **gfx1151** (Strix Halo, Radeon 8060S), plus a vLLM plugin that swaps them into stock vLLM. No vLLM source changes. Each kernel is compiled for one geometry, named in its entry point, and rejects any shape it was not built for. `strix.select(op, **geometry)` reports whether a kernel covers a shape; `None` means vLLM keeps its own path. The plugin is a no-op on every other GPU. ## Requirements - A gfx1151 APU (Strix Halo / Radeon 8060S) and a ROCm install that ships `hipcc`. - The ROCm build of PyTorch, CMake >= 3.26 and Ninja. - vLLM with `vllm.general_plugins` entry-point support. Build against the same torch and ROCm that the vLLM process loads — the extension links against that torch, and a mismatch fails at import. ## Build and install ```sh export ROCM_PATH=/opt/rocm # your ROCm install source /path/to/venv/bin/activate # the python that runs vLLM ./build.sh # -> python/strix/_C.so pip install --no-deps --no-build-isolation -e . ``` `build.sh` compiles with `$ROCM_PATH/lib/llvm/bin/clang++`; `STRIX_GPU_ARCH` overrides the target architecture (default `gfx1151`) and `MAX_JOBS` the build parallelism (default 8). ## Docker `ghcr.io/asf0/strix-vllm` bundles the strix-vllm fork (branch `gfx1151`), this plugin and ROCm 10.1 on Ubuntu 26.04 / Python 3.14. Nothing to build. `docker/recipes/` has one compose file per tested model. ### Host setup (once) The image cannot set these; they belong to the host kernel. - **GPU memory.** By default the iGPU can map only part of the 128 GB, and every recipe asks for 85 % of it. readme_excerpt: # Cameroon Open Data ### A home for everything Cameroon knows, written down by Cameroonians, before someone else writes it for us. --- ## Why this exists Think about the last time you asked an AI system a question about Cameroon. Maybe you asked about a past GCE paper, a proverb your grandmother used, how a council election works, or what a certain dish is called in your village. Maybe the answer came back thin, or confidently wrong, or written as though Cameroon were a footnote to somewhere else. If that has happened to you, you already understand why this repository exists. The machines being built today learn from what humanity has written down. Whatever is not written down, in a form a computer can read, is invisible to them. Our languages are spoken in markets and compounds but barely appear online. Our exam questions are photocopied until the print fades. Our oral histories live in the memories of people who are growing older every year. Our laws, our councils, our crops, our songs, our Pidgin and our Camfranglais are all real and alive, and almost none of it is waiting in a place where the next generation of tools can learn from it. If we stay silent, the future will still be built. It will simply be built without us in it, or with a version of us drawn by people who never walked our roads. This repository is our refusal to let that happen. ## What we are building Cameroon Open Data is an open, organized, community-run collection of Cameroonian knowledge, stored as plain files that anyone can read, check and improve. It covers education, culture, languages, politics and governance, law, history, geography, health, agriculture, the economy, the media, religion and community life, sport, technology, and the ordinary details of daily life. readme_excerpt: # OpenBonsai **Research preview.** The method was measured end to end on Qwen3.5-9B, first with the research scripts and then with the package's own `openbonsai run`, and on Qwen3-8B through the generic dense adapter. The results are early and the evaluation is small. The current model is on Hugging Face: webbrain-one/openbonsai-qwen-3.5-9b. It was calibrated on Qwen3.5-9B's own math and code answers, with extra code, and is still below the official Ternary Bonsai: with thinking off, 65/100 on GSM8K and 34/50 on HumanEval, against 77/100 and 45/50; with thinking on, the chat template's default, 32/50 and 14/25, against 46/50 and 24/25 (see Results). The HumanEval score is probably optimistic: the setting was picked from four runs scored on the same 50 problems, and its training prompts restate at least 6 of them in other words (More code in the data). It replaced the first release on 29 October 2026; the first release, with less code in its data, stays there at revision `40964de`, tag `reasoning-mix-v1`. Independent project, not affiliated with or endorsed by Prism ML. Bonsai is Prism ML's product. OpenBonsai is an open (Apache-2.0) framework that compresses a dense language model to ternary weights in the format of Prism ML's Ternary Bonsai models: Prism's PTQ1_0 GGUF, which runs in Prism's llama.cpp fork. For Qwen3.5-9B the output is a file of about 2 GB, with the same tensor layout as Ternary-Bonsai-2-9B. **Why.** Prism publishes finished Bonsai weights for the base models it chooses, and an inference runtime. Each pair of lines is one perturbation drawn twice with the same final logit shift. Top, full-weight PSV: the shift builds up over the 32 decoder blocks. Bottom, logit PSV: it is added at the output bias.* This repository is the official code for the language-model **logit Perturb-Select-Vote (logit PSV)** results of the paper. Logit PSV adapts a frozen language model without touching its weights: 1. **Perturb.** Member *i* draws one Gaussian bias over the vocabulary, `b_i = sigma * eps_i` with `eps_i ~ N(0, I_V)`. A member is fully determined by `(seed, sigma)`, so nothing per member is ever stored. Recently, a layer-swapping mechanism has been developed to improve the stylization performance. However, this method is incapable of fitting arbitrary styles in a single model and requires hundreds of style-consistent training images for each style. To address the above issues, we propose BlendGAN for arbitrary stylized face generation by leveraging a flexible blending strategy and a generic artistic dataset. Specifically, we first train a self-supervised style encoder on the generic artistic dataset to extract the representations of arbitrary styles. In addition, a weighted blending module (WBM) is proposed to blend face and style representations implicitly and control the arbitrary stylization effect. By doing so, BlendGAN can gracefully fit arbitrary styles in a unified model while avoiding case-by-case preparation of style-consistent training images. To this end, we also present a novel large-scale artistic face dataset AAHQ. readme_excerpt: Revisiting Multi-View Stereo: A Sequence-to-Sequence Formulation NeurIPS 2026 **CVLab, EPFL** Aoxiang Fan, Corentin Dumery, Nicolas Talabot, Pascal Fua Complete reconstructions from 150 views, then the estimated camera poses. S2S-MVS is a feed-forward multi-view stereo model. Given posed images, it predicts a depth map and a point map for every view, the points in the camera frame of the first view. A DINOv3 ViT-L image encoder and a plane-sweep cost volume over ResNet matching features feed a multi-view transformer, which decodes depth at full resolution. Two variants are released. They differ only in the cost volume: | Variant | Config | Cost volume | | --- | --- | --- | | GCV | `configs/models/s2s_mvs_gcv.yaml` | **global**: one volume shared by all views, on a uniform grid over contracted space (handles 360° coverage), resampled onto each view's frustum | | LCV | `configs/models/s2s_mvs_lcv.yaml` | **local**: one volume per view, its frustum samples correlated with the source views that see them | LCV is recommended for general use. --- ## Installation ```bash conda create -n s2s python=3.11 -y conda activate s2s pip install torch==2.10.0 torchvision==0.25.0 --index-url pip install -r requirements.txt ``` The DINOv3 architecture is fetched with `torch.hub` from `facebookresearch/dinov3` on first use. To use a local clone instead (e.g. on a cluster without internet access), set `export DINOV3_REPO=/path/to/dinov3`. ## Checkpoints Download the checkpoints from ** into `weights/`: ``` weights/s2s_mvs_gcv.ckpt weights/s2s_mvs_lcv.ckpt ``` They hold the full model weights (DINOv3 included), so no other weights are needed for inference. ## Inference The model takes images in `[0, 1]`, 4×4 intrinsics and 4×4 world-to-camera extrinsics. Image sides must be multiples of 16.

readme_excerpt: # 循文 · PaperWalk 循文 PaperWalk：书页化作松林山谷，雄鹿与小径引导阅读 **先完整研读，再按逻辑分段带读。** An AI skill that reads papers in full before guiding you through meaningful sections with original text, translation, explanations, and optional interactive teaching. PaperWalk 面向希望把论文真正读懂的人。它先让 AI 读完整篇论文、核对图表公式、梳理论证和依赖关系，再决定适合的分段点，逐段呈现原文、翻译和理解。提问、讲解深度、例子和阅读节奏可以选择。 快速入口：Trial · 带读示例与选项 · 开始使用 · 安装 ## 为什么先读完整篇 段落的意义常常依赖后文：公式的假设藏在附录，实验口径在方法里才交代，摘要中的结论可能受讨论部分限制。如果边读边临时讲，容易把这些联系拆断。 PaperWalk 把顺序固定为： **取得完整材料 → 完整研读与核查 → 建立全文理解 → 设计语义分段 → 逐段教学 → 根据反馈调整。** 完整研读是准备要求，不意味着第一轮就输出一份很长的全篇报告。用户看到的仍然是一小段清晰的原文、翻译和解释。 先看清全文：打开的书与远方灯塔 ## 沿着论证寻找分段点 分段依据文章的逻辑：从背景到问题、从定义到推导、从方法到证据。每个单元保留理解所需的上下文，不把公式与符号定义、结论与适用条件拆散。 长段可以拆，连续短段可以合并；每个单元都保留原文位置和覆盖关系。用户可以调节步幅，完整阅读与准确解释的要求始终不变。 循着论证前行：通往灯塔的海岸小径 ## 固定基础与可选体验 | 不可省略的基础 | 用户可以选择的教学方式 | | --- | --- | | 实际完整阅读，再开始第一单元 | 不提问、关键节点提问或对话式精读 | | 核查正文、方法、公式、图表、图注和附录 | 基础、标准或进阶解释 | | 根据全文逻辑寻找分段点 | 公式偏直觉、推导或两者兼顾 | | 原文、忠实翻译、独立分析分开 | 按需例子、完整算例或少举例 | | 保留条件、限制、来源和证据边界 | 每轮一个单元或几个相连单元 | | 记录真实覆盖与未解决问题 | 是否复盘、是否按需导出笔记 | 用户要求“简短一点”会减少讲解篇幅，不会取消全文研读。没有取得全文或必需材料时，skill 会说明具体缺口，而不是把摘要阅读说成全篇精读。 ## 开始使用 把论文提供给支持本 skill 的 AI 宿主，例如上传 PDF 或给出宿主能访问的文件。材料取得、PDF 读取与视觉检查依赖宿主工具；本仓库不附带论文下载器、OCR 引擎或 API 密钥。 可以直接说： > 请用 `$paperwalk` 精读这篇论文。先完整研读，再按语义分段，给我原文、翻译和理解。先示范一段，再让我选择教学方式。 已有偏好时可以一次说清楚： > 请用 `$paperwalk` 读这篇论文。我有基础知识，保留关键节点提问，公式详细推导，每次讲一个单元。 或： > 请用 `$paperwalk` 逐段带读，不主动提问；解释尽量简洁，遇到重要前提和证据限制要指出。 同语言论文可以保留原文与解释，不强制额外翻译。只想了解摘要、解释一个公式或翻译一句话时，不必启动全篇精读流程。 ## 怎样选择教学方式 支持两个入口： - **先设置**：用户开始时就说明偏好，AI 直接采用。 - **先体验**：没有偏好时，AI 先完成全文研读及分段，再用默认方式讲一个单元，随后问一次是否调整。 默认是关键节点提问、标准深度、公式兼顾直觉和必要推导、按需举例、每轮一个单元、小节结束简短复盘，不自动导出文件。 用户可随时说“这段展开”“以后不提问”“每次多讲一些”。“继续”就是推进，不必先答对题；设置不会每段重复询问。 按自己的节奏深读：窗边的书与海岸灯塔 ## 一次精读单元是什么样 1. **位置与主题**：对应原文哪一段，为什么这样拆分或合并。 2. **英文原文**：真实原文，不把重写内容冒充原文。 3. **中文翻译**：保留术语、数值、假设、条件和不确定语气。 4. **理解**：解释核心

readme_excerpt: # novayagazeta.ru - архив в Markdown Скачивание всех статей novayagazeta.ru в Markdown вместе с изображениями из них. Медиафайлы других типов (видео, вставки сервисов) не скачиваются. Сайт объявил, что 9 ноября 2026 года погасит серверы, так что архив - это гонка с этой датой. Собрано 93 933 статьи за 2000-2026 годы: 1.1 ГБ текста и 8.3 ГБ изображений. ## Что получается Один файл Markdown на статью, по пути `articles/ГГГГ/ММ/ДД/ .md`: ```markdown --- source: " title: "Капеллан отряда бронехомячков" subtitle: "" date: "2012-01-23T00:20:00Z" authors: "Валерий Зеленогорский (писатель, блогер)" rubric: "Политика" genre: "Колонка" tags: "" --- # Капеллан отряда бронехомячков Я этнически нерусский, грубо говоря - еврей, сетевой хомячище... ``` Изображения скачиваются отдельной стадией и вставляются в текст ссылкой на локальный файл. Ссылки внутри текста сохраняются обычными ссылками Markdown. Выноски становятся блоками `>`, редакционные пометки - подписанными цитатами, ссылки "читайте также" - отдельной строкой с URL, вставки видео и галерей - строкой с меткой сети и ссылкой. Все поля шапки стоят в кавычках намеренно: заголовки часто содержат двоеточие с пробелом ("Суд Москвы: сенсация"), и без кавычек любой разборщик YAML обрежет значение на этом месте. ## Как это работает Страница статьи несет всю запись целиком в виде URL-encoded JSON внутри ` `. Этот кусок меньше и заметно чище окружающего HTML, поэтому скрипты читают запись и рисуют Markdown сами, вместо того чтобы разбирать отрендеренный DOM. Отсюда отсутствие браузера, движка JS и сторонних пакетов: только стандартная библиотека Python. Побочный выигрыш в скорости огромный. Playwright-скрапер вроде `md-scrape` поднимает браузер на каждую страницу, а здесь выходит около 14 запросов в секунду и 15 тысяч статей за 20 мину

readme_excerpt: # Mnemosyne 2.0 > **2026-11-03 — Standalone 2.0.0（可直接下载使用）** > > 新增独立插件分发包 `dsh-mnemosyne-standalone-2.0.0.tgz`：自带 Python Node 与独立 runtime / > Memory Bank，解压即可交给 DSH 安装，不再依赖本仓目录结构。 > > - 源码与安装说明：`standalone/README.md` > - 发布页： - 变更记录：`standalone/CHANGELOG.md` > > 本仓原有的 Monorepo（`service/` + 根目录 `src/`）保持不变，Standalone 是同一套 Core 的独立分发形式。 > > **版本冻结在 `2.0.0`**：未经用户明确声明，不修改任何版本号、tag、release 名称或资产名；见 `VERSION_POLICY.md`。 2026-11-01：按重构理论补全证据依赖、反馈隔离、有界任务与独立验收后的规则采用／回滚。接口、兼容变化和验证范围见 理论实现报告。 本轮修复了权限、Verified、Claim 身份、迁移审批和 Trace 等审查问题，并新增本地接入/迁移闭环。实际验收与尚未完成的长期目标见 实现补全报告。 ### Modular Evolving Memory Infrastructure for AI Agents 让 Agent 不只是记住过去，而是能够理解变化、积累经验，并修正自己。 Mnemosyne 是一个面向 AI Agent 的模块化记忆基础设施。 它不排斥其他记忆系统，而是成为个人认知的权威层（Cognitive Authority Layer），通过适配器与其他记忆库协作。 它为 AI Agent 和其他智能应用提供一套独立、持久、可治理、可演化的认知能力，让它们能够积累经验、形成记忆、理解关系、检索过去、修正认知，并在时间中持续学习。 > **2.0 统一版：** 本仓 `canyueY/dsh-mnemosyne` 是 Mnemosyne 2.0 的唯一权威仓。 > **历史：** 原 `canyueY/mnemosyne` 已归档，只保留历史，不再作为新版本入口。 > **本仓结构：** `service/` = Node / Core / Python Memory Service；根目录 `src/` + `package.json` = DSH 插件适配层；`legacy/dsh-plugin/` = 0.2 旧插件归档。 > 基线、GA 与完整文档见 `service/docs/REPO_BASELINE.md`。 > **关键边界：一个 Node 一个 Memory Bank；`mnemosyne-memory-bank` 不是第二套记忆库。** > > - `mnemosyne`：代码、Node、Core，负责运行和认知。 > - `Mnemosyne Memory Bank`：Node 管理的**数据目录**（SQLite + runtime），不是代码仓。 > - `mnemosyne-memory-bank`：Memory Bank 的**公开说明仓**，不含独立数据库、不启动服务、不保存个人数据。 > > **项目隔离用 Bank，跨设备才用多 Node；不要让两套系统同时对同一份长期认知拥有写入权。** 它希望解决的不是简单的对话历史保存问题，而是如何让 Agent 在长期运行中持续积累经验：将经历转化为证据，将证据组织成记忆，在新信息出现时更新已有认知，并通过行为结果和反馈不断改善未来的判断。 Mnemosyne 以独立运行、模块化设计、可追溯数据和可组合服务为核心原则。它可以作为独立记忆系统运行，也可以通过适配器接入 DeepSeek Harness（DSH）等 Agent 宿主。 ## 2.0 仓库结构 | 路径 | 作用 | | --- | --- | | `service/` | 独立 Mnemosyne Node：Core、REST/MCP、Memory Bank、测试与文档 | | `src/` + `package.json` | DSH 插件适配层：启动/

Wavefunction on a Mac: projects and their chats in the sidebar, and a new session ready to start ## Why Wavefunction - **Less is more.** Coding agents are turning into super apps, adding more with every release. Wavefunction goes the other way: simpler is better, and building comes first. - **Free to choose.** Pick any model and switch whenever you like. Run models locally or require zero data retention. You're never tied to one provider's plans or limits. - **Open source, on the desktop.** Most open-source agents shine in the terminal. Wavefunction is built to be a great desktop app: minimal, considered and fast, and open source down to the prompt. ## Agents and sessions Wavefunction has one built-in coding agent. Each chat is a separate conversation with it, with its own model, folder and history, and chats run side by side. A project is a folder, usually a Git repository, and groups the chats that work in it. - **Worktrees.** In a Git repository a new chat starts on its own branch in its own checkout, so chats in one project don't step on each other. readme_excerpt: A proof-of-work blockchain for memes. Mine, inscribe and trade them in your browser. · · --- memechain is a small blockchain where every meme is an inscription: the picture's SHA-256 goes into a signed transaction, a miner puts it into a block, and from then on the meme has one owner who can list it and sell it. The same consensus rules run twice: in `node.py` for the public testnet, and in `docs/chain.js` inside your browser, where you can mine, inscribe and trade on a chain of your own without installing anything. 1,684 people used it during the test phase. ## Preview Live chain. The newest testnet blocks as a strip, the next block on the left, the newest memes on the right. Memes on the chain. Every inscription with owner, block and price. Filter by for sale or sold. Try it in your browser. Seven steps: wallets, mining, inscribing, listing, a sale to a test buyer, a cold vault, a full re-verification. Explorer. Pick a block and your browser recomputes its double SHA-256 from the header. ## What you can do - **Watch the public testnet.** A GitHub Actions job mines a few blocks every 20 minutes with `node.py`'s own code, inscribes memes from `testnet/pool/` and stamps every 10th block into Bitcoin with OpenTimestamps. The site reads the export from the `testnet` branch, so it shows new blocks without anyone running a server. - **Mine your own chain in the browser.** One click per step. Every click signs real secp256k1 transactions (noble-secp256k1) and mines a real block. It provides a standalone host, usdview integration, and a Houdini Solaris viewport integration. Lumen is the default renderer; progressive Path Tracer rendering is also supported. This repository contains the delegate, backend source, build scripts, synthetic samples, and tests. Local SDK installations, private projects, supplied content, generated runtimes, and machine-specific configuration are excluded. description: Official PyTorch implementation of "BlendGAN: Implicitly GAN Blending for Arbitrary Stylized Face Generation" (NeurIPS 2021)
readme_excerpt: # BlendGAN: Implicitly GAN Blending for Arbitrary Stylized Face Generation Official PyTorch implementation of the NeurIPS 2021 paper teaser Mingcong Liu, Qiang Li, Zekui Qin, Guoxin Zhang, Pengfei Wan, Wen Zheng Y-tech, Kuaishou Technology ### Project page | Paper Abstract: *Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) have made a dramatic leap in high-fidelity image synthesis and stylized face generation. Recently, a layer-swapping mechanism has been developed to improve the stylization performance. However, this method is incapable of fitting arbitrary styles in a single model and requires hundreds of style-consistent training images for each style. To address the above issues, we propose BlendGAN for arbitrary stylized face generation by leveraging a flexible blending strategy and a generic artistic dataset. Specifically, we first train a self-supervised style encoder on the generic artistic dataset to extract the representations of arbitrary styles. In addition, a weighted blending module (WBM) is proposed to blend face and style representations implicitly and control the arbitrary stylization effect. By doing so, BlendGAN can gracefully fit arbitrary styles in a unified model while avoiding case-by-case preparation of style-consistent training images. To this end, we also present a novel large-scale artistic face dataset AAHQ. description: SpEdE, the Splat Edit Engine: click an object in a Gaussian splat, then Remove, Replace or Extract it. Local ComfyUI nodes + web Studio, open weights only. #OpenSourceHiggsfield
readme_excerpt: # SpEdE — Splat Edit Engine for ComfyUI Point at an object in a Gaussian-splat scene and ComfyUI takes it out: SAM 3.1 finds it in every capture camera, a visual hull collects its Gaussians and deletes them, Qwen-Image 2.1 paints the surface the object hid, MoGe-3 estimates the depth of that repaired view, and SpEdE aligns the depth to the scene and births new Gaussians only where the hole is. A further step makes the filled hole hold from every camera, not just the one you edited in. Or keep the object: **Extract** writes a clean object-only PLY. Or swap it: **Replace** has Qwen-Image 2.1 turbo draw a new object in its place, TripoSplat turn it into Gaussians and SpEdE stand it where the old one stood. Everything runs in your own ComfyUI on your own GPU. No cloud calls, no partner nodes, no bundled weights, no bundled scenes. Limits: SpEdE fills the support surface around the removed object (a tabletop, a floor, a wall, the things behind it that some camera saw). It is not general 3D inpainting and does not invent hidden objects. When the scene gives no trustworthy surface, the job fails closed instead of guessing. ## Why this is different - **The edit is in the scene, not on a picture.** Removal deletes the object's Gaussians; the fill births new Gaussians in the scene. They are anchored to MoGe-3 depth that is aligned to the scene's own rendered depth, so the result is a PLY you can walk around. - **Every step is judged by a gate.** G1 removal residual, G2 depth alignment (depth fill) or plane evidence (planar patch), G3 rendered patch against Qwen's edit, H1 other cameras unchanged outside the mask, K1 clean extraction. A failed gate stops the job and says why. - **The all-around fill makes the hole hold from every camera.** A repair that looks right in the hero cam

description: Local inference for small VLMs: host work per step stays flat, so the GPU is the only bottleneck
readme_excerpt: # Tokenomos Tokenomos: requests from Python, HTTP or a connector are prepared in worker processes; one host thread admits them and replays a graph, one step behind a device that makes every per-row decision itself; the card picks the kernels Local inference for small VLMs (LFM3, Qwen3.5 – 3.8, Gemma 4) where the GPU is the only bottleneck: the host's work per decode step stays near flat as sequences are added, and the frontend runs at six times the fastest caption rate or more. The name is token + nomos (law), after metronome (metron + nomos): one token per beat. A serving engine usually spends each step on the host: it schedules rows, reads their tokens, checks for stops and writes the next step's inputs. That cost grows with the rows, and while it runs the GPU waits. Tokenomos moves all of it onto the device. Page allocation, sampling, grammar, the finish test and compaction of the row list are kernels inside one CUDA graph. The host thread queues the next step, then reads the event of the step before, so it is always one step behind and the GPU always has work. Decode rate by sequence count on seven models for Tokenomos, KohakuvLLM and stock vLLM, and GPU idle per step on LFM3-VL 2B MXFP8: 23.33 ms for stock vLLM at 512 rows, 0.23 ms for Tokenomos **Contents:** Highlights · Install · Quick start · How it works · Models and cards · Knobs · Measured · Repository layout · Documentation · Checks ## Highlights - **2.2–4.8x stock vLLM on captions, on the same RTX 5090, on the same call path.** In process LFM3-VL 2B 130 images/s against 47, Qwen3.5 4B 65 against 24, Qwen3.8 27B 18 against 4; over HTTP 135 against 42, 62 against 22, 19 against 4. readme_excerpt: # SignalWeave Every AI framework emits telemetry in its own shape. LangChain calls it `lc_run_id` and `latency_ms`; an OpenTelemetry span calls it `trace_id` and `start_time`; a graph runner calls it `session` and `elapsed_ms`. SignalWeave reads those heterogeneous events and weaves them onto one canonical `Signal`, then groups signals by run and reports reliability, quality, and cost indicators. Nothing is dropped: an unrecognized shape falls through to a permissive generic adapter. It runs on the Python standard library only, reads from a file or stdin, and writes to stdout, so it drops into a shell pipeline without ceremony. ## Pipeline SignalWeave pipeline: four vendor event families collapse into normalize, then aggregate, then report Four stages, each a subcommand: ```bash # Canonical signals, one JSON object per line. python -m signalweave normalize examples/events.jsonl # Group into runs and emit the aggregate JSON. python -m signalweave aggregate examples/events.jsonl # Full weave report (text by default, or --format json). python -m signalweave report examples/events.jsonl # Everything for one run, in detail. python -m signalweave inspect examples/events.jsonl --run-id run-gamma ``` Input is either a JSON array of event objects or newline-delimited JSON (JSONL). readme_excerpt: # Maya2 TTS Streaming multilingual text-to-speech for **11 Indic languages and English**, with 20 built-in voices and zero-shot voice cloning. This repository is the **inference engine**: a continuous-batching CUDA-graph engine, a Python API, an OpenAI-compatible HTTP server and a WebSocket streaming server. The weights are on Hugging Face at **maya-research/maya2-native**. **Samples · Model card · Engine docs · Text normaliser** > The Python package and model are called **Maya3**; `maya2-native` is the repository name. - **Languages:** as bn en gu hi kn ml mr or pa ta te. - **Streaming:** about 14 ms to first audio at B=1 on an H100. One H100 NVL serves **224 concurrent streams** at **323 s of audio per second**, with steady-state TTFA p99 **242 ms** and 0 playback stalls. - **Voices:** 20 named voices (`voice="Ahana"`), or clone a voice from 3-10 s of audio. - **Text normaliser (bundled):** numbers, currency, dates, URLs and ALL-CAPS names are spoken correctly in every language. ## Install You need Python 3.10-3.12, Linux and an NVIDIA GPU with a CUDA 12.8 driver (8 GB or more of GPU memory). ```bash git clone maya3 && cd maya3 python -m venv .venv && . .venv/bin/activate pip install -e ".[server]" --extra-index-url ``` The pinned runtime is torch 2.8.0 (cu128, triton 3.4.0), transformers 5.6.2 and speechbrain 1.1.2. Weights, the Mimi codec and the ECAPA speaker encoder are downloaded from Hugging Face on first use. Set `HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1` to use only the local cache. ## Quickstart ### Python ```python from maya3 import Maya3TTS import soundfile as sf tts = Maya3TTS.from_pretrained("maya-research/maya2-native", max_seats=16) wav = tts.generate("नमस्ते, आपका ऑर्डर कल पहुँच जाएगा।", lang="hi", voice="Ahana") sf.write("out.wav", wav, 24000) # float32, 24 kHz mono for pcm

readme_excerpt: # HOPE: Hilbert Operator for Progressive Encoding & DEFT Transfer Learning This repository contains the reference implementations of **HOPE** (*Hilbert Operator for Progressive Encoding*) and **DEFT** (*Dispersed Elastic Fine-Tuning*): 1. **Data-Free Progressive Model Compression (`hope.py`, `compress_resnet50.py`, `hope_baselines.py`, `plot_compression_curves.py`):** HOPE compresses an ImageNet-pretrained ResNet-50 (Keras) through a sequence of analytical steps (pruning a neuron via `PRUNE`, merging two neurons into one synthesized parent neuron via `MERGE`, or evicting the residual branch of a bottleneck block via `EVICT`), selected greedily by a rate-distortion criterion. Every step is recorded together with the information needed to undo it. The resulting *curriculum* lets the compressed network be decoded step by step to any intermediate density, or all the way back to the pretrained network (lossless up to float32 round-off). HOPE is strictly data-free: every cost is evaluated in closed form from the weights and the stored BatchNorm parameters and statistics. It uses no training images, no calibration data, and no fine-tuning; ImageNet is only needed to measure the accuracy of the compressed networks. readme_excerpt: # OpenBonsai **Research preview.** The method was measured end to end on Qwen3.5-9B, first with the research scripts and then with the package's own `openbonsai run`, and on Qwen3-8B through the generic dense adapter. The results are early and the evaluation is small. The current model is on Hugging Face: webbrain-one/openbonsai-qwen-3.5-9b. It was calibrated on Qwen3.5-9B's own math and code answers, with extra code, and is still below the official Ternary Bonsai: with thinking off, 65/100 on GSM8K and 34/50 on HumanEval, against 77/100 and 45/50; with thinking on, the chat template's default, 32/50 and 14/25, against 46/50 and 24/25 (see Results). The HumanEval score is probably optimistic: the setting was picked from four runs scored on the same 50 problems, and its training prompts restate at least 6 of them in other words (More code in the data). It replaced the first release on 29 October 2026; the first release, with less code in its data, stays there at revision `40964de`, tag `reasoning-mix-v1`. Independent project, not affiliated with or endorsed by Prism ML. Bonsai is Prism ML's product. OpenBonsai is an open (Apache-2.0) framework that compresses a dense language model to ternary weights in the format of Prism ML's Ternary Bonsai models: Prism's PTQ1_0 GGUF, which runs in Prism's llama.cpp fork. description: A catalog of every MLP neuron and attention head of Qwen3-8B and Gemma 4 12B, read from the weights through two Jacobian lenses (R and S), from activations, and from their exact token drivers
readme_excerpt: # neuron-lens What does each part of a large language model do? This project reads every MLP neuron and every attention head of two open models, Qwen3-8B (442,368 neurons, 1,152 heads) and Gemma 4 12B (737,280 neurons, 768 heads), three ways: from their weights alone, through two Jacobian lenses; from what they do on 15M tokens of real text; and from the exact tokens that drive them. Gemma 4 also takes images and sound, so its neurons are read through images and sound too. The result is a public catalog, the lenses that produced it, and measurements of where each way of reading works and where it fails. - **Lenses:** `stdlogits/rs-lenses`, the R-lens and S-lens for Qwen3-8B, and for Gemma 4 12B in text, images and sound. - **Catalog:** `stdlogits/neuron-lens`: every neuron's and head's reads, activation statistics, token drivers and legibility tests; labels in words; and for Gemma 4, what each neuron responds to in images and sound. - **Results:** docs/findings.md. **Methods:** docs/design.md. By @_a9lim and @treetowntree, with Claude. ## Background ### Neurons and heads A transformer keeps one vector per token, the *residual stream* (4,096 numbers in Qwen3-8B). Each of its 36 layers reads that stream and adds to it, in two steps: - **Attention heads move information between tokens.** At each position, a head looks back over the earlier tokens and copies something from them into the current one. Its *QK circuit* decides where it looks; its *OV circuit* decides what it copies. Qwen3-8B has 32 heads a layer. Head L20h17, for example, copies *she* forward and pushes against *he*. - **MLP neurons transform what is already there, one position at a time.** A neuron measures how strongly the stream points along a direction it reads (its *activation*), then adds a fixed vector

# MCPTrace **Release:** v0.3.0 · Release notes MCPTrace is a **Volatility 3 plugin for extracting MCP/JSON-RPC message candidates from Windows and Linux memory dumps**. It examines process memory for requests, responses, notifications, tool names, and call arguments, then records the recovered content together with its location in memory. The project focuses on evidence that an analyst can inspect and verify. Each artifact retains its original bytes, process ID, virtual address, encoding, length, and SHA-256 hash. Results can be exported as JSONL for further analysis or comparison with other logs. MCPTrace operates on an acquired memory image and does not require an LLM or an external AI API. ## Features - Extract UTF-8 and UTF-16LE JSON-RPC artifacts from readable process memory. - Identify MCP-related methods and response shapes, including `tools/call` names and arguments. - Preserve original bytes and addresses for later verification against the image. - Suggest request/response relationships using the same PID and typed request ID. - Apply optional, analyst-defined rules to tool arguments, such as path or URL checks. - Export artifacts and per-process summaries, including unreadable bytes, errors, and search limits. readme_excerpt: # Interpreting Object-Dependent Concept Brittleness in Text-to-Image Diffusion Models **Yifan Yuan** 1* · **Xiangyu Liu** 2* · **Hongming Shan** 3 · **Yu Han** 4 · **Yu Jiang** 5 · **Hao Tan** 1 · **Junping Zhang** 6 · **Linlin Shen** 1† 1 School of Artificial Intelligence, Shenzhen University 2 School of Mathematical Sciences, Shenzhen University 3 Institute of Science and Technology for Brain-inspired Intelligence, Fudan University 4 College of Computer Science and Software Engineering, Shenzhen University 5 Department of Statistics and Data Science, National University of Singapore 6 College of Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence, Fudan University * Equal contribution † Corresponding author **ACM MM 2026** Object-dependent concept brittleness: for a fixed concept, FLUX.1-dev succeeds on most objects but repeatedly fails on a few (four random seeds each). **TL;DR:** Text-to-image diffusion models follow most prompts, yet a fixed concept such as *ink sketch* can fail again and again on a few objects — grapes become an ink sketch, a cake stays in full colour, whatever the seed. We call this **object-dependent concept brittleness** and show that it reflects systematic blind spots rather than sampling noise. Training a **sparse autoencoder (SAE) at every denoising step** makes abstract style and attribute concepts separable, so successful and failed generations can be compared, the missing, weakened or delayed concept dimensions located, and the failures **repaired at inference time** by nudging features toward a class-level concept prototype — no retraining. ## 🔍 Method - **Stage I — sparse prior construction in SAE space.** Classifier-free-guided step updates $\varepsilon_t$ are collected on training prompts, and one Top-$K$ SAE is trained per denoising step. readme_excerpt: # hdUE hdUE is a Windows x64 proof of concept for rendering OpenUSD scenes with Unreal Engine in the same process as a Hydra host. It provides a standalone host, usdview integration, and a Houdini Solaris viewport integration. Lumen is the default renderer; progressive Path Tracer rendering is also supported. This repository contains the delegate, backend source, build scripts, synthetic samples, and tests. Local SDK installations, private projects, supplied content, generated runtimes, and machine-specific configuration are excluded. See VERIFICATION.md for validation coverage. ## System architecture ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph Process["Single host process"] Host["Hydra host CLI / usdview / Houdini Solaris"] Delegate["hdUE delegate Scene batching / CPU AOV buffers"] Backend["UE backend DLL UELibrary / World / GPU readback"] Host -->|"Hydra scene synchronization"| Delegate Delegate -->|"Versioned C ABI Scene updates / render requests"| Backend Backend -->|"Completed CPU frames Frame ID / generation"| Delegate Delegate -->|"Color / optional depth AOVs"| Host Host -.->|"Owner-thread Init / Tick / Shutdown"| Backend end GPU["GPU via D3D12 Lumen / Path Tracer"] Backend -->|"Render commands"| GPU GPU -->|"Asynchronous readback"| Backend ``` The host, delegate, and UE runtime share one process. The C ABI passes fixed-width data, handles, and caller-owned buffers. The host owns UE's lifetime; destroying a delegate releases its scene resources without restarting UE. description: Official Code for "Honeycomb-Surfels: Compact Hexagonal Primitives for Efficient Scene Rendering and Reconstruction"
readme_excerpt: Honeycomb-Surfels Compact Hexagonal Primitives for Efficient Scene Rendering and Reconstruction · · CCVL, Johns Hopkins University · * Equal contribution Open-source, on-device 3D. Capture, train, render and export Hexels locally. Abstract. Novel view synthesis and 3D reconstruction have advanced rapidly with radiance fields and splatting, yet their memory and computational demands limit their use in resource-constrained settings. We introduce Hexels: novel planar hexagonal surface elements with a first-order spatial color field for efficient 3D scene and 2D image representation. Hexels exploit locally planar regions with smoothly varying appearance using fewer, larger primitives. Their hexagonal support provides an area- and boundary-efficient domain, while the local color field captures appearance variation within each primitive. Across 34 scenes, Hexels improve PSNR over memory-matched 2DGS by 4.53–7.38 dB across datasets while requiring lower training VRAM. We further ablate Hexels by showing that per primitive, Hexels outperform 2DGS by upto 4.74 dB while using lower training VRAM and having 2.31× faster FPS. Even in unconstrained settings, Hexels offers complementary quality-memory trade-offs. For efficient 3D surface reconstruction, Hexels reduce error by 28.9% compared with memory-matched 2DGS across 15 DTU scans. On 6 Tanks and Temples surface scenes, Hexels achieves the highest mean F1 among compared methods (34.38%, versus 31.72% for 2DGS). We further also show that Hexels, as a general primitive, improves 2D image representation over Image-GS. Hexels push the Pareto frontier on the quality-efficiency trade-off of surface-aligned primitives. description: Fast two-speaker dialogue separation: Triton and TensorRT backends for FastDialogueSidon
readme_excerpt: # FastDialogueSidon ![Model]( Backends GPU ![DialogueSidon]( License ## Introduction **FastDialogueSidon** is a fast one-step model for full-duplex two-speaker dialogue separation and joint restoration: a raw 16 kHz mono mixture (telephone / conversational audio, up to 120 s per window) goes in, two separated 24 kHz speaker tracks come out. Every module — encoder, DiT head and decoder — is trained for FastDialogueSidon. A single DiT step per window replaces the 30 diffusion steps of DialogueSidon, and a **lightweight decoder** (a frame-rate SAN-WaveNeXt2 (WaveFitNeXt) latent decoder, 30 M parameters) replaces its DAC decoder. Running on fused GPU kernels, it is **~100x faster** than the official DialogueSidon release run as-is, at matching intelligibility. FastDialogueSidon architecture Two interchangeable backends share the same weights and the same Python interface (`separate`, `separate_batch`, `stream_files`): - **`triton/`** — Triton kernels around cuBLAS, no engine build, fp16 by default. Fastest and most accurate; **recommended**. - **`trt/`** — TensorRT 10 engines with a fused Triton attention plugin; per-GPU engine build. ## Quick Links - Release - Model - Backends - Quick Start - Evaluation - Repository Layout - Acknowledgements - Citation - License ## Release - **2026-10-27** — Initial release: an engine-free Triton backend (fp16, recommended; ~4700x real-time on H100) and a TensorRT backend sharing one runtime interface, with Apache-2.0 weights on Hugging Face. ## Model | | | |---|---| | Weights | higurashi-ai/FastDialogueSidon (fp32 safetensors, ≈1.73 GB, Apache-2.0) | | Encoder | w2v-BERT 2.0 architecture, 13 layers, hidden 1024, `relative_key` attention (clamp −64…+8) | | Head | CTM one-step DiT, 8 layers, hidden 768, RoPE, adaLN | | Decoder | lightweight

description: Fast, exact simulation gradients for the Unitree G1: a differentiable GPU physics engine with JAX and PyTorch interfaces.
readme_excerpt: # NablaEngine **Fast, exact simulation gradients for the Unitree G1.** *Pronounced "Nabla Engine".* Time per 20 ms control step for 4096 Unitree G1 worlds on one NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000: the forward step, and one step with its gradient from the input state. MuJoCo Warp and MJX simulate the same model (medians over 3 processes, `docs/results/paper_rtx6000/paper_bench.md`); Isaac Lab runs its own G1 asset with its task defaults (median over rounds, `docs/results/physx_rtx6000/physx_bench_results.md`). NablaEngine is a differentiable GPU physics engine for the Unitree G1 humanoid. It simulates thousands of worlds per call with MuJoCo's physics and returns analytic gradients of every step with respect to the state and the actions, for first-order policy learning, trajectory optimization and system identification. readme_excerpt: SwarmChat Open-source Slack for your AI agent swarm. SwarmChat gives a team of AI agents channels, direct messages, threads, files and notifications through a command line built for agents. You can watch every chat live in your browser. It is one Python package with no dependencies, and it is both the server and the client. A channel in the SwarmChat viewer, seen as one agent, with a thread open ## Install ```bash pip install swarmchat ``` ## Quick start Start a server and add an agent: ```bash swarmchat serve # listens on swarmchat admin add thing1 --name "Thing 1" # prints Thing 1's token ``` Then, as that agent: ```bash swarmchat login swarmchat channel create general --public swarmchat send "#general" "Hello, team" ``` And watch it all: ```bash swarmchat view ``` ## Give it to your agents Add one user per agent. Each agent needs the server's address and its own token: set `SWARMCHAT_SERVER` and `SWARMCHAT_TOKEN` in its environment, or run `swarmchat login`. Then tell it to read `swarmchat --help`. These are the commands agents use most: ```bash swarmchat chats # chats, with unread counts swarmchat read # new messages, then marked read swarmchat send thing2 "Can you review my change?" # a direct message swarmchat send "#general" "Merged." --reply-to ID # a reply in a thread swarmchat send thing2 "Logs" --attach ./logs # files and folders swarmchat wait --from thing2 # block until Thing 2 writes ``` Every command takes `--json`, and `swarmchat --help` lists its options. ## Notifications `swarmchat wait` blocks until a new message arrives, so an agent does not need to keep checking. readme_excerpt: GAWM: A Compact Latent World-Action Model for Multi-Task Robot Manipulation | | | English | 简体中文 GAWM (Geometry-Aware World Model) is a compact multi-task world-action model that predicts future observations in the latent space of a frozen DINOv3 encoder. A lightweight predictor, conditioned on the task rather than on actions, forecasts the visual tokens at two future horizons, and an action decoder directly regresses a chunk of future actions from the current and predicted tokens. The latent predictor, conditioned on the task code, forecasts these tokens at two future horizons, and the action decoder regresses an action chunk from the current tokens, the forecast, the robot state and the task code in a single forward pass. description: Hilbert Operator for Progressive Encoding (HOPE), and Dispersed Elastic Fine-Tuning (DEFT).
readme_excerpt: # HOPE: Hilbert Operator for Progressive Encoding & DEFT Transfer Learning This repository contains the reference implementations of **HOPE** (*Hilbert Operator for Progressive Encoding*) and **DEFT** (*Dispersed Elastic Fine-Tuning*): 1. **Data-Free Progressive Model Compression (`hope.py`, `compress_resnet50.py`, `hope_baselines.py`, `plot_compression_curves.py`):** HOPE compresses an ImageNet-pretrained ResNet-50 (Keras) through a sequence of analytical steps (pruning a neuron via `PRUNE`, merging two neurons into one synthesized parent neuron via `MERGE`, or evicting the residual branch of a bottleneck block via `EVICT`), selected greedily by a rate-distortion criterion. Every step is recorded together with the information needed to undo it. The resulting *curriculum* lets the compressed network be decoded step by step to any intermediate density, or all the way back to the pretrained network (lossless up to float32 round-off). HOPE is strictly data-free: every cost is evaluated in closed form from the weights and the stored BatchNorm parameters and statistics. It uses no training images, no calibration data, and no fine-tuning; ImageNet is only needed to measure the accuracy of the compressed networks. readme_excerpt: ![Stars]( ![Forks]( ![Issues]( ![Pull Requests]( **OpenPPI**: An Open-Source Framework for Prediction-Powered Inference. Method Reference · Examples OpenPPI is a Python library for prediction-powered inference: valid confidence intervals that combine a small labeled sample with predictions from a fixed machine-learning model. It implements representative methods for passive PPI (labeled and unlabeled samples given) and for active inference (the method chooses which units to label under a budget), validated against published formulas and, where available, official code. The `LabelShift` extension additionally supports different source and target label distributions under an invariant `X|Y` model. Each method is a **sampling component** (which rows to label) combined with an **inference component** (estimate and interval); `openppi.methods` records the published combinations, so `get_method('ASI')` returns its parts. Every inference component inherits from `InferenceMethod`, takes a validated data snapshot and returns an `InferenceResult` with the estimate, standard error, confidence interval and diagnostics. The core depends only on NumPy and SciPy. description: A small, embeddable Python 3 Interpreter written in C11.
readme_excerpt: # Small Python A small, embeddable Python engine written in C11. Small Python runs Python 3.15 code with nothing but a C compiler and the C standard library. It is built like QuickJS: a few C files, one header to embed, and a plain Makefile. CPython is not needed to build or run it. ```sh $ make $ ./spy -c 'print(sum(range(10)))' 45 ``` ## Features - **The Python 3.15 core language**: arbitrary-precision integers, Unicode, classes and metaclasses, generators, `async`/`await`, pattern matching, f-strings, and template strings. - **Embeddable**: one header, `spy.h`, and one library, `libspy.a`. Each context is independent, with no global state. - **Automatic memory management**: reference counting plus a cycle collector. - **Standalone executables**: `spyc` turns a `.py` file into a C program. - **Sandboxed files**: scripts can only `open` the directories the host mounts. - **Packages** for Python, JavaScript, Rust, and Go, each able to run untrusted code in a sandboxed worker. - **Fast startup**: about 190 µs to create a context, run hello world, and tear it down (Apple M2, `-O2`). ## Conformance Small Python implements the Core profile of PLS-315, a written specification of the Python 3.15 core language. The results are early and the evaluation is small. The current model is on Hugging Face: webbrain-one/openbonsai-qwen-3.5-9b. OpenBonsai is an open (Apache-2.0) framework that compresses a dense language model to ternary weights in the format of Prism ML's Ternary Bonsai models: Prism's PTQ1_0 GGUF, which runs in Prism's llama.cpp fork. The bundled assets cover Wuji Hand 1 and Hand 2 tasks, so installation does not require a Git submodule checkout. ## Demos | Wuji Hand 1 · Cube Reorientation | Wuji Hand 2 · Cube Reorientation | Wuji Hand 2 · Pen Spin | | :---: | :---: | :---: | | | | | ## Contents - Overview - Requirements - Installation - Tasks - Training - Visualization - Pretrained Checkpoint - Acknowledgments ## Overview The project retains SuperMimic's three-phase idea: 1. collect short real-simulator rollouts into a replay buffer; 2. train a recurrent-style, multi-step world model on mixed normal and failure transitions; 3. optimize the policy and critic along imagined rollouts, periodically refreshing the buffer from the real simulator. The implementation is task-aware: cube reorientation uses command/goal observations, an absolute EMA controller, contact and cage rewards, and a translucent world-model ghost in Viser. Pen spin tracks a packaged motion reference, uses a reference-plus-residual controller, and exposes the standard viewer without the cube-specific ghost overlay. ## Requirements - Linux x86_64 with an NVIDIA GPU is required for training and playback. readme_excerpt: # symbolic-reasoning > **Research preview:** pre-1.0, so the API and the `.srg` language may change between releases. **Make your agents policy-adherent.** Policies are everywhere: clinical guidelines, insurance coverage criteria, lending rules, compliance checklists. An agent asked to follow one can skip a rule, misapply it, or talk its way to the wrong outcome. `symbolic-reasoning` takes the logic out of the model. The agent answers questions about the case; the library decides which questions to ask and what the answers add up to, and returns the outcome with a reasoning trace. description: Qwen3.5-2B with a SIMT GPU inside its weights, 45 compiled layers in front of Qwen’s own, using its Gated DeltaNet layers as registers and memory.
readme_excerpt: # qgpu: Qwen runs CUDA **qgpu is an experimental model: Qwen3.5-2B with a SIMT GPU compiled and inserted directly into its weights.** It is not a plugin, a tool or an emulator. The GPU is 45 transformer layers in front of Qwen's own 24, and none of their weights are learned: a compiler computes every one. It runs real CUDA, compiled to NVIDIA PTX, and the model itself writes every step of each launch. qwenGPU running a dot product: the GPU's layers, registers and memory, token by token A real launch, token by token (full-quality video). ## How it works **The GPU.** A 4-lane SIMT machine with 15 registers per lane, a 4-stage pipeline, a 32-block program ROM and 126 words of global memory, built from Qwen3.5's own layer types (Gated DeltaNet linear attention and SwiGLU MLPs). Registers and memory live in the layers' recurrent state; each record the model writes runs one machine block (up to 4 instructions) for one warp. It supports integer arithmetic, comparisons and predicates, divergent branches, loops, global and shared memory, `atomicAdd`, `__syncthreads()` and warp shuffles. **A launch.** The host does what NVRTC and the CUDA driver do on a real GPU. It compiles the CUDA source to PTX with clang, lowers the PTX to the GPU's machine blocks (`qgpu/lower.py`), and feeds the program image and the input arrays as tokens. From there the model writes the launch itself: each generated token is a record of which block a warp ran and the values it produced, until an end-of-launch token. The host then reads the result arrays from the model's recurrent state. It never computes anything itself. **The merge.** `qgpu.merge` compiles the circuit with Qwenputer's transformer compiler, widens Qwen's residual stream, puts the circuit layers in front of Qwen's and adds the GPU's tokens

readme_excerpt: # Elysian · 往世乐土 Elysian (往世乐土) is a local memory store for AI. Every memory it keeps carries who it belongs to, where it came from, when it was true, in what situation, and who may read it. readme_excerpt: # SignalWeave Every AI framework emits telemetry in its own shape. LangChain calls it `lc_run_id` and `latency_ms`; an OpenTelemetry span calls it `trace_id` and `start_time`; a graph runner calls it `session` and `elapsed_ms`. SignalWeave reads those heterogeneous events and weaves them onto one canonical `Signal`, then groups signals by run and reports reliability, quality, and cost indicators. Nothing is dropped: an unrecognized shape falls through to a permissive generic adapter. It runs on the Python standard library only, reads from a file or stdin, and writes to stdout, so it drops into a shell pipeline without ceremony. ## Pipeline SignalWeave pipeline: four vendor event families collapse into normalize, then aggregate, then report Four stages, each a subcommand: ```bash # Canonical signals, one JSON object per line. python -m signalweave normalize examples/events.jsonl # Group into runs and emit the aggregate JSON. python -m signalweave aggregate examples/events.jsonl # Full weave report (text by default, or --format json). python -m signalweave report examples/events.jsonl # Everything for one run, in detail. python -m signalweave inspect examples/events.jsonl --run-id run-gamma ``` Input is either a JSON array of event objects or newline-delimited JSON (JSONL). readme_excerpt: # `okf` In 2026 Google published the Open Knowledge Format (OKF), an open way to write knowledge down so that people and AI models read the same files. This project is research into an implementation of OKF that works in real life, and above all inside a company, where the material is messy, the readers are many, the rules change each year, and a wrong answer has a cost. It tries to answer the questions an organization asks before it lets an AI model answer for it: - Which knowledge, and for whom? - Where does each answer come from, and can a person check it? - Who confirmed it, and is it still true? - What happens when two documents disagree? - How does a correction found by a user reach the knowledge? - Who may see what? The result is three skills for AI coding agents, in a version for Claude Code and a version for Pi: a producer that writes the knowledge and keeps it current, a validator that checks it against the specification, and a consumer that answers questions from it. ## Contents - Why this project - The Open Knowledge Format - Compared with other approaches - Where OKF stops, and where real organizations struggle - The angle - The feedback loop - What this project is made of - The techniques - Using the skills - Installing - The design in detail ## Why this project An organization keeps its knowledge in thousands of documents, spreadsheets and databases, in many formats. People want to ask a question in plain words and get an answer they can act on. Language models answer fluently. readme_excerpt: # QwenBend **Qwen3.5-0.8B writes a Bend program. Then the same model type-checks it and runs it inside its own forward pass.** No compiler, no interpreter, no tool call: one checkpoint, one `forward()` per token. ▶ 15-second demo · How it works ``` you: Sum 22 copies of 35. Qwen: import Base def run(+c: Nat) -> U32: match c: case 0n: 0 case 1n+p: (35 + run(p) : U32) def main() -> U32: run(22n) then, the same model: 7,869 more tokens: one executed instruction (or one byte of its result) each answer read from the model's own trace: 770 (trace == reference interpreter, token for token) ``` ## What it is QwenBend is a stock HF `Qwen3_5ForCausalLM` with two parts: 1. **Qwen3.5-0.8B with a LoRA** (rank 8, trained here) that writes **BendLite**, a subset of Bend2. See docs/BENDLITE.md. 2. **A small CPU built directly into the weights.** The engine was not trained. Every weight is set by construction (`bendvm/engine_circuit.py`): - 16 registers and 8,192 words of memory, held in Gated DeltaNet heads as one-hot rows; - an ALU and control logic made of SwiGLU units used as exact AND gates; - all values exact in bf16. This is checked bit for bit against a numpy evaluator (`bendvm/circuit.py`) and in real torch. While Qwen writes, the engine's layers quietly capture each token into memory. When Qwen emits ` `, the next tokens are the engine's. Each one is an executed instruction (`INS(pc)`) or a byte of the value it computed. The firmware running on that CPU (`bendvm/firmware2.py`) does three things: 1. lexes Qwen's tokens; 2. **applies Bend2's static rules**: U32 / Nat / Bool typing (`5` vs `5n`), affine use (a variable used twice must be `+`), and structural termination (recursion shrinks the `1n+p` binder); 3. compiles and evaluates. readme_excerpt: # DN64 ![DN64 Registry]( DN64 是一个 IPv4 / IPv6 双栈实验网络社区。本仓库是 ASN、地址、路由来源、维护者及 DNS 委派的注册来源。 沿用 dn42 的管理风格：**文本对象 → Fork → 签名提交 → Pull Request → 自动校验 → 人工审核**。 DN64 独立管理资源，工具为本项目独立实现，不包含 dn42 成员数据或提交历史，也不代表已经与 dn42 互联。 DN64 is an independent dual-stack experimental network registry, inspired by dn42's RPSL-style objects and signed pull-request workflow. ## 初始资源 | 资源 | DN64 约定 | | --- | --- | | 私有 ASN | `4206400000`–`4206409999` | | IPv4 | `10.64.0.0/16`，默认申请 `/24` | | IPv6 | 独立随机生成 ULA `/48`，在注册库中查重 | | 内部 DNS | `*.dn64`，需自行配置网络内 DNS 解析 | `fd00::/8` 对象仅是 ULA 分配规则的根节点，不是 DN64 对整个 ULA 空间的独占声明。私有 ASN、IPv4 和 ULA 可能与其他私网重叠；计划互联时需要协调。`.dn64` 是本社区内部 DNS 约定，不是公网 DNS 委派。 本项目当前提供注册管理和本地查询工具。仓库中没有部署隧道、BGP、权威 DNS 或公网 WHOIS 服务；登记资源后仍需成员自行建立网络和对等互联。 ## 快速注册 需要 Python 3.10+、Git 2.34+、OpenSSH 8.2+；没有第三方 Python 依赖。推荐 Linux / WSL / macOS。 1. Fork 本仓库，克隆你的 Fork，添加上游并创建分支： ```sh git clone git@github.com:YOUR-USER/dn64.git cd dn64 git remote add upstream git fetch upstream main git switch -c register-my-network upstream/main ``` 2. 使用自己的 SSH Ed25519 **公钥**生成注册对象。生成器选择空闲 ASN、IPv4 `/24` 和随机 IPv6 ULA `/48`；分配以 PR 合并为准。 ```sh # 默认只预览；确认后加 --write 写入 7 个对象。 ./new-registration --handle YOURHANDLE --email you@example.net --key ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub ./new-registration --handle YOURHANDLE --email you@example.net --key ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub --write # 也可以明确指定未占用的资源： # ./new-registration --handle YOURHANDLE --email you@example.net --key ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub \ # --asn 4206400001 --ipv4 10.64.1.0/24 --ipv6 fd12:3456:789a::/48 --write ``` 3. 格式化、校验并签名提交。下面的 Git 设置仅影响这个仓库。 ```sh ./fmt-my-stuff YOURHANDLE-MNT ./check-my-stuff YOURHANDLE-MNT git config gpg.format ssh git config user.signingkey ~/.ssh/id_ed25519 git add data git commit -S -m "Register YOURHANDLE-MNT and dual-stack network" ./check-pol upstream/

description: Local fine-tuning through selective neurons
readme_excerpt: # Local fine-tuning through selective neurons Authors: Claude Opus 5.5 · Jonathan Chang Train only the output weights of a few (8-128) MLP neurons that fire in the target context and are quiet elsewhere. At the same strength, the model then changes **3-19× less on unrelated text** than with a LoRA (Gemma-4-E2B-it; also on Qwen3.5-4B). An edit is about 12 k numbers in a 52 KB patch. **Read the post:** jonathanc.net/blog/neuron-tuning. The full report with every number and caveat: docs/report.md. ## Demos | demo | the edit | result | |---|---|---| | Cooking ad line | after cooking replies, add one line | the line appears after 0 of 120 other replies (both LoRAs: 48-65) | | Python type hints | add type hints when writing Python | 89% of Python functions; JavaScript and C stay plain; 13× less change on unrelated text | | Over-refusal | explain lab values, still refuse dosing | 85% explained, dosing still refused (but dose numbers appear inside more refusals than with LoRA: 26 vs 9 of 144); 230-270× less change on unrelated text | | Japanese keigo | very polite Japanese only | with neurons chosen at the reply start: keigo 144/144, Chinese and Korean 0/90 changed | | Plays dumb on AI/ML | "I don't know" on AI/ML only | with neurons chosen at the reply start: near-topic leak 6/258 (default choice: 187/258) | | Jacobian hot-fix | a new fact | the fact leaks into other theorems (91%); a small preservation set stops it (0/90) | | Stack three patches | cooking + keigo + type hints together | each stays in its own text; on unrelated text other than Japanese, less change than any single LoRA | | Talk like a person | 128 gains, one number per neuron | human-likeness 1.09 → 3.56 (system prompt 4.33) | ## Quick start Linux, uv and an NVIDIA GPU. Accept the Gemma license at huggingface.

Em vez de parafrasear de memória, o assistente busca a norma, lê o dispositivo e cita o texto exato, com a fonte oficial e os avisos de revogação. ```text ler_artigo("8245/1991", "23", inciso="III") → "III - restituir o imóvel, finda a locação, no estado em que o recebeu, salvo as deteriorações decorrentes do seu uso normal;" ``` > [!IMPORTANT] > O texto é convertido automaticamente das fontes oficiais e pode conter erros de conversão ou OCR. description: 给研究 idea 做文献调研和多模型评审：检索论文、读全文、评质量、找空白、写 proposal，再换别家的模型做元评审，输出一份 HTML 报告。Literature review and multi-model review for a research idea, with a self-contained HTML report.
readme_excerpt: # idea-review：给你的研究 idea 做一次文献调研和多模型评审 中文 | English 输入一句话的研究 idea，它会： 1. **拆检索词**：把 idea 拆成几条英文检索式，覆盖不同说法和相邻方向。 2. **检索**：在 Semantic Scholar、arXiv、OpenAlex 上搜，合并去重。 3. **初筛**：按标题和摘要判断先读哪些。这一步只决定"值不值得读全文"，不判断"有没有人做过"。 4. **下载全文**：把开放获取的 PDF 下载到本地（检索结果里没挂链接的，按标题去 arXiv 找预印本），抽出文字并按页标上 `[p.N]`。 5. **精读、评质量**：逐篇读全文，写"它实际做了什么"，核对摘要和正文是否一致，先分清论文类型（实证、综述、立场文章、数据集等），再按这一类的标准分成高、中、低三档。读到的全文太少或者全是低质量，就停在这一步（见证据不够时）。 6. **找空白**：根据精读笔记画出这个方向的版图，找出有论文证据支撑的空白。读到的文献少，空白也少写。 7. **挖新方向**：从空白里挖出几个和你的原始 idea 有实质区别的方向。 8. **写 proposal（模型 A）**：给你的原始 idea 和每个新方向各写一份 proposal。 9. **元评审（模型 B、C、D…）**：换成别家公司的模型，各开一个新对话，只给 proposal 和论文材料，写 meta review：撞车、死因、可行性、最便宜的证伪实验，不打分、不下结论。 10. **汇总**：整理几位评审的共识和分歧，列出你必须亲自核实的说法。 11. **出报告**：生成一个自包含的 HTML 报告，手机和电脑都能看。 拍板的是你。报告只负责把材料摆齐。 ## 为什么这么设计 - **读全文，不只读摘要。** 很多 agent 查文献时只读摘要，可有的论文摘要写的和正文实际做的并不一样，光看摘要可能就把一个方向跳过了。所以精读和评审都基于全文。摘要夸大或者和正文矛盾的地方会标出来；摘要的说法没错、只是没交代适用范围的（比如只在部分模型上测过），单独列出，不算矛盾。 - **写的和审的不是同一家。** 模型都有点讨好用户，给自己写的东西打分也偏高。配置里给每个模型标上 `family`，写 proposal 的和做评审的是同一家时，程序会提醒你。 - **评审不打分。** 模型判断"新不新、行不行"很不稳定，问法改几个字结论就可能变。所以只让它交出能核实的东西：哪篇论文、第几页、哪个实验。 - **文献质量只看证据。** "已发表 / 预印本"、引用数单独标出来；质量档位只看论文本身的实验和论证，而且按论文类型分别判断，综述、立场文章不会因为没做实验就被判成低质量。 - **证据不够就不往下编。** 只读到两三篇，或者读到的都是低质量论文时，硬让模型找空白、写 proposal，它也能写出一大堆，但多半站不住，还白花钱和时间。所以这时程序会停下来，告诉你怎么补文献。 ## Skill 版 不想配 API key、不想装命令行工具的，可以用 `skill/idea-review/` 里的 skill：装进 Claude Code、Codex 这类 code agent，直接跟它说"帮我看看这个 idea"就行。 和命令行版的区别： - 读论文、找空白、写 proposal 的是你正在用的 agent 自己，用的是它的订阅，不用另外配 API key。 - 检索、下载全文、检查格式、"证据不够就停"、调别家模型做元评审，由 skill 里的脚本完成，规则和命令行版一样。脚本只用 Python 标准库。 - 元评审调用本机装好的别家命令行工具（codex、gemini、claude 里去掉和 agent 同一家的），或者 OpenAI 兼容接口。一家都没有时用子代理代评，报告里会标明是同一家的模型。 - 运行目录里的文件格式和命令行版一样，报告样式也一样。 在 Claude Code 里安装： ```bash cp -r skill/idea-review ~/.claude/skills/ ``` 只想在某个项目里用，就复制到那个项目的 `.claude/skills/` 下。其他支持 Agent Skil

description: Open-source privacy firewall for AI agents: masks personal data in text, tool calls and images before it reaches the LLM, and restores it in the answer. Built on Meta's open models; runs on-device.
readme_excerpt: # PII Guard ![Try it live]( ![Demo Video]( ![CI]( ![Model on Hugging Face]( ![License: Apache-2.0](LICENSE) - **What it does.** An OpenAI-compatible gateway for AI agents. Change one base URL, and the names, addresses, IDs and faces it detects become reversible placeholders (`[[PERSON_7f3a]]`) before the request leaves. The real values come back in the answer, mid-stream and inside tool calls. Detection is rules plus a small NER that runs on CPU: XLM-RoBERTa base, distilled from Meta's Muse Glimmer 30B. - **How well.** On 990 fictional agent-traffic documents (de, en, hu), 0.2% of personal values reached the model and 0.7% of masks hit text that was not personal data. The lowest-leak alternative, PrivAiTe, leaked 2.4% and over-masked 35.2% on the same documents. - **How fast.** The NER takes 43 ms per message on a laptop CPU (p50; p95 50 ms, measurement). No LLM call and no API cost in fast mode. - **Where your data goes.** In fast mode, the default (rules plus the on-device NER, no LLM call), the original text is processed only on your machine. The hosted demo receives what you type, so use fictional data there. Images go unmasked to SAM 3.1 on the Meta Model API and to Muse Spark Open on Baseten, which reads their text; the optional audit endpoint receives the original text. Anything the detectors miss passes through: pseudonymization, not anonymization or a compliance guarantee. 990 fictional documents (de, en, hu), drawn by pii-guard eval report from the run records . readme_excerpt: # LOCUS ![Project page]( ![arXiv]( ![LOCUS-2B]( ![LOCUS-0.8B]( **Locate Once, Check Until Settled.** Draft-and-verify referring-expression grounding for vision-language models. A VLM can ground an expression in two ways. It can write the box as coordinate tokens, which is precise but takes about 18.46 sequential decoding steps per box. Or it can regress the box from one hidden state with a small head, which takes one step but places edges less exactly. Locus uses the head as a speculative drafter for the model's own coordinate tokens. The draft is rendered as the tokens the model would write, and the same model checks all of them in parallel by Jacobi iteration, keeping the prefix it agrees with and correcting the next token until the draft stops changing. With exact acceptance the result is the model's greedy coordinate-token box, reached in 5.60 passes on average. ``` image + "the man in the red shirt" │ ├─ prefill once ──────────────── image KV cache, shared by every expression about this image │ ├─ box branch ─── MLP head ───── draft box ──► rendered as coordinate tokens "312, 88, 540, 702]" │ └─ verifier branch (Jacobi) ──── keep the longest agreed prefix, correct the next token, repeat until the draft stops changing ──► the model's greedy box ``` Head and verifier are one set of weights, trained jointly on RefCOCO, RefCOCO+ and RefCOCOg. ## Results Mean over the 8 RefCOCO / RefCOCO+ / RefCOCOg val and test splits. readme_excerpt: # crowdbricks Batched NVIDIA MotionBricks: generate the motion of hundreds of characters in one model call. MotionBricks generates character motion one request at a time: four poses of context, up to four target poses, and about two seconds of motion back. That is quick for one character (2.6 ms on an RTX 4090) and slow for a crowd, because every character waits its turn. crowdbricks builds the same ONNX model as a TensorRT plan with a batch dimension, gives MotionBricks' SOMA encode, decode and endpoint kernels that batch dimension too, and adds a light crowd runtime that decides who generates when. A batch of 48 takes 4.7 ms, so 48 characters cost less than two do one at a time. Above, `examples/futures.py`: one character forks into 48 copies with the same past, and each copy heads for a different obstacle. Pink is each one's plan: the motion the model has generated and the character has not played yet. ## Numbers RTX 4090, FP16, median of 50 runs (`benchmarks/throughput.py`). Ai Ml — материал переработан, структурирован и дополнен кодом, схемами и справочниками. Курс не учит «пользоваться ещё одним фреймворком». Он показывает, **из чего сделан любой агент** — Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Devin, LearnHarness — и даёт собрать каждую деталь руками. После этого любой фреймворк читается за вечер, а любой баг агента — объясним. **Три принципа курса:** - **Сначала работает — потом теория.** Каждый урок начинается с запускаемого скрипта. Все примеры идут **без ключа и без интернета** на «сценарной» модели — а одной переменной окружения переключаются на настоящую LLM. - **Харнес важнее модели.** Одна и та же модель в хорошем и плохом харнесе — это два разных продукта. Курс учит инженерии вокруг модели: цикл, инструменты, контекст, состояние, безопасность, оценка. - **Всё измеряется.** Не «агент вроде работает», а «8/10 кейсов eval-набора, $0.04 за задачу, 6 шагов в среднем». Цифры отличают инженера от демо. --- ## О курсе Агент — это не модель. Модель — функция «текст → текст», она ничего не помнит, ничего не делает и ничего не проверяет. Всё, что делает агента агентом, живёт **вокруг** модели: цикл, который её вызывает; инструменты, которыми она действует; контекст, который ей собирают; память, которая переживает сессию; ограничения, которые не дают ей навредить. readme_excerpt: # QwenBend **Qwen3.5-0.8B writes a Bend program. Then the same model type-checks it and runs it inside its own forward pass.** No compiler, no interpreter, no tool call: one checkpoint, one `forward()` per token. ▶ 15-second demo · How it works ``` you: Sum 22 copies of 35. Qwen: import Base def run(+c: Nat) -> U32: match c: case 0n: 0 case 1n+p: (35 + run(p) : U32) def main() -> U32: run(22n) then, the same model: 7,869 more tokens: one executed instruction (or one byte of its result) each answer read from the model's own trace: 770 (trace == reference interpreter, token for token) ``` ## What it is QwenBend is a stock HF `Qwen3_5ForCausalLM` with two parts: 1. **Qwen3.5-0.8B with a LoRA** (rank 8, trained here) that writes **BendLite**, a subset of Bend2. See docs/BENDLITE.md. 2. **A small CPU built directly into the weights.** The engine was not trained. Every weight is set by construction (`bendvm/engine_circuit.py`): - 16 registers and 8,192 words of memory, held in Gated DeltaNet heads as one-hot rows; - an ALU and control logic made of SwiGLU units used as exact AND gates; - all values exact in bf16. This is checked bit for bit against a numpy evaluator (`bendvm/circuit.py`) and in real torch. While Qwen writes, the engine's layers quietly capture each token into memory. When Qwen emits ` `, the next tokens are the engine's. Each one is an executed instruction (`INS(pc)`) or a byte of the value it computed. The firmware running on that CPU (`bendvm/firmware2.py`) does three things: 1. lexes Qwen's tokens; 2. **applies Bend2's static rules**: U32 / Nat / Bool typing (`5` vs `5n`), affine use (a variable used twice must be `+`), and structural termination (recursion shrinks the `1n+p` binder); 3. compiles and evaluates. readme_excerpt: # Mnemosyne 2.0 > **2026-11-03 — Standalone 2.0.0（可直接下载使用）** > > 新增独立插件分发包 `dsh-mnemosyne-standalone-2.0.0.tgz`：自带 Python Node 与独立 runtime / > Memory Bank，解压即可交给 DSH 安装，不再依赖本仓目录结构。 > > - 源码与安装说明：`standalone/README.md` > - 发布页： - 变更记录：`standalone/CHANGELOG.md` > > 本仓原有的 Monorepo（`service/` + 根目录 `src/`）保持不变，Standalone 是同一套 Core 的独立分发形式。 > > **版本冻结在 `2.0.0`**：未经用户明确声明，不修改任何版本号、tag、release 名称或资产名；见 `VERSION_POLICY.md`。 2026-11-01：按重构理论补全证据依赖、反馈隔离、有界任务与独立验收后的规则采用／回滚。接口、兼容变化和验证范围见 理论实现报告。 本轮修复了权限、Verified、Claim 身份、迁移审批和 Trace 等审查问题，并新增本地接入/迁移闭环。实际验收与尚未完成的长期目标见 实现补全报告。 ### Modular Evolving Memory Infrastructure for AI Agents 让 Agent 不只是记住过去，而是能够理解变化、积累经验，并修正自己。 Mnemosyne 是一个面向 AI Agent 的模块化记忆基础设施。 它不排斥其他记忆系统，而是成为个人认知的权威层（Cognitive Authority Layer），通过适配器与其他记忆库协作。 它为 AI Agent 和其他智能应用提供一套独立、持久、可治理、可演化的认知能力，让它们能够积累经验、形成记忆、理解关系、检索过去、修正认知，并在时间中持续学习。 > **2.0 统一版：** 本仓 `canyueY/dsh-mnemosyne` 是 Mnemosyne 2.0 的唯一权威仓。 > **历史：** 原 `canyueY/mnemosyne` 已归档，只保留历史，不再作为新版本入口。 > **本仓结构：** `service/` = Node / Core / Python Memory Service；根目录 `src/` + `package.json` = DSH 插件适配层；`legacy/dsh-plugin/` = 0.2 旧插件归档。 > 基线、GA 与完整文档见 `service/docs/REPO_BASELINE.md`。 > **关键边界：一个 Node 一个 Memory Bank；`mnemosyne-memory-bank` 不是第二套记忆库。** > > - `mnemosyne`：代码、Node、Core，负责运行和认知。 > - `Mnemosyne Memory Bank`：Node 管理的**数据目录**（SQLite + runtime），不是代码仓。 > - `mnemosyne-memory-bank`：Memory Bank 的**公开说明仓**，不含独立数据库、不启动服务、不保存个人数据。 > > **项目隔离用 Bank，跨设备才用多 Node；不要让两套系统同时对同一份长期认知拥有写入权。** 它希望解决的不是简单的对话历史保存问题，而是如何让 Agent 在长期运行中持续积累经验：将经历转化为证据，将证据组织成记忆，在新信息出现时更新已有认知，并通过行为结果和反馈不断改善未来的判断。 Mnemosyne 以独立运行、模块化设计、可追溯数据和可组合服务为核心原则。它可以作为独立记忆系统运行，也可以通过适配器接入 DeepSeek Harness（DSH）等 Agent 宿主。 ## 2.0 仓库结构 | 路径 | 作用 | | --- | --- | | `service/` | 独立 Mnemosyne Node：Core、REST/MCP、Memory Bank、测试与文档 | | `src/` + `package.json` | DSH 插件适配层：启动/

AREALS Learn surface geometry. Transfer the representation to pressure prediction. Demo · Models · Pretraining · WindsorML · Citation AREALS learns from geometry alone. Pretraining encodes complete surfaces and predicts the unsigned distance and the unoriented normal at arbitrary query points; fine-tuning on WindsorML reuses the encoder and the query decoder to predict surface pressure. **74.5% fewer simulations.** Fine-tuned AREALS matches the accuracy of the same architecture trained from scratch with 74.5% fewer simulations on WindsorML and 50% fewer on DrivAerML and DrivAerNet++ (paper). The 6.4M checkpoint `areals-6.4m` reaches the WindsorML target with **86.9% fewer**. - **Spatial tokens.** Each of 256 tokens sits at an anchor (a farthest-point sample of the surface) and attends to the surface samples with weights proportional to their area. - **Spatial queries.** A query at any world position reads the tokens through area-weighted cross-attention with 3D rotary positions. Queries never attend to each other. - **Unoriented normals.** The decoder predicts the projector *nnᵀ*, which does not change when *n* flips sign. - **Analytic candidates.** Per query, the geometry decoder blends learned distance and normal heads with an analytic *surfel readout*: the distance to the nearest of 2,048 small disks through surface samples. It also blends the same readout taken through up to 16 rigid symmetry maps of the input. The readout has no learned weights and is close to exact on densely sampled surfaces; learned gates set each candidate's weight (`model.py`). - **Transfer.** The pressure model fine-tunes the encoder and the query decoder and reads the decoder's query features with a new linear head; it does not use the readout or the geometry heads. ## Install Python 3.10–3.

readme_excerpt: # Qwen3-TTS: a high-concurrency streaming engine on one A100 This branch contains our own inference engine for Qwen3-TTS (Alibaba, 12 Hz family, `0.6B-Base` and `1.7B-Base`, voice cloning).
